hypotheses.justification: When `v ≥ n`, `p.pos[v]!` defaults to 0. If `n = 0`, `Refines` is vacuous. Otherwise, `hp` ensures position 0 belongs to the cell starting at 0, and `individualize` only changes `cst` entries within that first cell, where `hp.cellCst` shows the old values are 0. Thus no old cell start is lost. A proof can split on `v < n`: use the existing argument in that case, and unfold `individualize` and `setCstFrom` to establish preservation for the default-index case.
